title: Could You Possibly...?

pre.en: What does Arjun think of Chen's email?
pre.zh: Arjun 觉得小陈的邮件怎么样？
options: It is more formal than it needs to be.

intro: 一段室友之间的对话：小陈刚加入 Rachel 的团队，要找负责后端的 Arjun 要 API 文档。Rachel 提醒他，直来直去的说法在英语里像下命令，于是他写了一封客气得过了头的邮件，还把室友 Tom 拉来帮忙。读的时候留意 I hope …、I'm afraid …、I was wondering if … 后面怎么接一个完整的句子，再看看 Arjun 的回复有多随意。

sentences.en: Tom, could you give me a hand with an email?
sentences.zh: Tom，能帮我看看一封邮件吗？
sentences.speaker: Chen

sentences.en: He's in charge of the backend.
I need the API document as soon as possible.
sentences.zh: 我得尽快拿到 API 文档。

sentences.en: So just ask him for it.
sentences.zh: 那直接找他要不就完了。
sentences.speaker: Tom

sentences.en: But Rachel says "Send me the API document" sounds like an order in English.
sentences.zh: 可 Rachel 说，「Send me the API document」这种说法在英语里听着像下命令。

sentences.en: Well, she's right, to be honest.
sentences.speaker: Tom

sentences.en: Actually, I've gone a bit further than that.
sentences.zh: 其实我加的可不止一个 please。
sentences.speaker: Chen

sentences.zh: 「尊敬的 Arjun：希望您一切安好。」

sentences.en: "My name's Chen, and I've just joined Rachel's team."
sentences.zh: 「我是小陈，刚加入 Rachel 的团队。」

sentences.en: "I'm afraid I have a small favour to ask."
"I was wondering if you could possibly send me the API document."
sentences.zh: 「不知您能否发我一份 API 文档。」

sentences.en: "I've been reading an old version since Monday, but I'm not sure whether it's still up to date."
sentences.zh: 「我从周一起一直在看一份旧版本，但不确定它现在还是不是最新的。」
sentences.speaker: Chen

sentences.en: "Would you mind looking over my questions when you have time?"
sentences.zh: 「您有空的时候，能否帮我看看我的问题？」

sentences.en: "I know you're in the middle of a busy week, so there's no need to reply straight away."
sentences.zh: 「我知道您这周正忙，所以不必马上回复。」
sentences.speaker: Chen

sentences.en: "On the other hand, I can't make a decision about the login screen without the latest version."
sentences.zh: 「不过话说回来，没有最新版本，登录页的事我没法做决定。」

sentences.en: "Could you get back to me when you're free?"
sentences.zh: 「您方便的时候能否回复我一下？」

sentences.en: Anyway, make sure there are no mistakes before you send it.
sentences.zh: 总之，发之前检查一下有没有写错。

sentences.en: "My flatmate Tom has been helping me for an hour, so I hope there are no mistakes."
sentences.zh: 「这封邮件我室友 Tom 已经帮我弄了一个小时，所以希望没有写错的地方。」

sentences.en: "PS: You don't have to be that formal."

sentences.zh: 「直接说 Can you send it? 就行。」

cards.note: to help someone, especially with a practical job
cards.tip: 比 help 口语；帮什么用 with：give sb a hand with sth。主动提出帮忙可以说 Do you need a hand?
cards.example: Can you give me a hand with these boxes?

cards.note: responsible for a person, group or piece of work
cards.tip: 人做主语：he's in charge of the backend；前面的 be 不能丢。take charge of 是「接手、接管」。
cards.example: Who's in charge of the release this week?

cards.note: as quickly as you can
cards.tip: 邮件里常缩写成 ASAP，语气比较急；想客气一点，可以说 when you get a chance（你方便的时候）。
cards.example: The app keeps crashing, so we need a fix as soon as possible.

cards.note: 这里不是「订单」。give an order 下命令；sound like an order 听着像在下命令。
used before you say what you really think, especially something the listener may not like
used to say that a bad situation has one good point; not less than
英式拼写，美式写 favor。开口求人常说 Can I ask you a favour?；帮某人一个忙是 do sb a favour。
放在 could you 后面，让请求更客气：Could you possibly …? 平时的意思是「可能」：It's possibly the best app I've used.
放在名词前要加连字符：an up-to-date version；反义是 out of date（过时的）。
to read or examine something quickly in order to check it
cards.tip: look over 是快速过一遍，逐条细看一般说 go through；代词常放中间：Could you look it over?
cards.example: Could you look over my pull request before lunch?

cards.note: during something, or at the centre of a place
used to introduce a different or opposite point
cards.tip: 用来和前一句对比，常放句首、后面加逗号；单独用就行，前面不一定要有 on the one hand。
cards.example: The new laptop is fast. On the other hand, it's very expensive.

cards.note: to choose what to do after thinking about it
to reply to someone later, by phone, email or message
cards.tip: to 不能丢：get back to sb。「回复你」不说 reply you，要说 reply to you；工作里最常听到的是 I'll get back to you。
cards.example: Let me check with the team and get back to you this afternoon.

cards.note: used to say that someone else should make the decision
before a particular time or event
cards.tip: Thanks in advance 是邮件常见结尾，但对方还没答应就先谢，有人会觉得像在催；不想有这层意思，写 Thanks for your help 更稳。
cards.example: Please send me the slides in advance so I can read them before the meeting.

cards.note: Kind regards / Best regards 都是常用落款，比 Best 正式；表示「问候」时总用复数：Give my regards to your team.
to do or check something so that you are certain it happens
cards.tip: 后面的句子说将来的事也用现在时：Make sure you call him tomorrow，不说 you will call。
cards.example: Make sure you save your changes before you close the file.

cards.note: postscript 的缩写，写在落款后面补一句。读作 /ˌpiː ˈes/，前面用 a。
反义是 informal 或 casual；a formal email 正式邮件。
to begin doing something
cards.tip: 比 start 口语；开始做什么用 on：get started on the new feature。开会时常说 Shall we get started?
cards.example: We'll get started when everyone has joined the call.
